items.original_ja: 惑星は恒星の周りを回る。
items.original_en: Planets move around a fixed star.
items.corrected_ja: お酒を飲みすぎて頭が回らない。
items.corrected_en: I drank too much and can't think straight.
items.notes: Replaced astrophysics terminology (恒星) with colloquial everyday usage (頭が回る / 駅前の店を回る).

items.original_ja: 愛の力は世界を動かす。
items.original_en: Love makes the world go round.
items.corrected_en: The power of love moves the world.
items.notes: Confirmed reading ちから; aligned English translation closer to 力.

items.original_ja: 父は田で働いています。
items.original_en: My father works in the rice fields.
items.corrected_ja: 春になると田に水を引く。
items.corrected_en: When spring comes, water is drawn into the rice fields.
items.notes: Nobody says 田で働いています in modern Japanese (people say 田んぼ). However, 田に水を引く / 田に水を入れる is natural modern usage with standalone 田.

items.original_en: Your husband is an office worker.
items.corrected_ja: 御主人はお元気ですか。
items.corrected_en: How is your husband doing?
items.notes: Telling someone 'Your husband is an office worker' makes no conversational sense. Changed to a natural greeting (note: modern orthography usually writes ご主人 in kana, though 御主人 is valid if the kanji token requires 御).

items.original_en: I woke up with a crick in my neck.
items.notes: Spot-on colloquial modern Japanese.

items.original_ja: ここは公共の乗り物が不便だ。
items.original_en: This place isn't convenient to public transportation.
items.corrected_ja: ここは駅から遠くてちょっと不便だね。
items.corrected_en: This place is far from the station, so it's a bit inconvenient.
items.notes: 公共の乗り物が不便だ sounds like a bad translation of 'public transportation'. Replaced with natural spoken Japanese.

items.original_ja: 台風の被害は数県にまたがっていた。
items.original_en: The damage of the typhoon spread over several prefectures.
items.corrected_en: The typhoon damage spanned several prefectures.
items.notes: Natural modern news/conversational Japanese.

items.original_en: The yen is still low against the dollar.
items.corrected_en: The yen keeps getting weaker, doesn't it?
items.notes: Super natural modern conversational Japanese (especially these days!). Updated the English so it captures 進んでいる (progressing/getting further weak).

items.original_en: Handsome is that handsome does.
items.corrected_ja: 彼の言葉が心に残った。
items.corrected_en: His words stayed with me.
items.notes: 見目 (みめ) is archaic. 心に残る ('stayed in my heart / stuck with me') is everyday modern Japanese.

items.original_en: I'm a junior high school student.
items.notes: WARNING: Header says わたくし, proposed reading says わたし. In modern Japanese, 私は中学生です is strictly わたし. If the database entry requires わたくし, replace sentence with: わたくしからご説明いたします ('I will explain it').

items.original_en: The entire town was under water.
items.corrected_en: The entire town was flooded.
items.notes: Natural modern Japanese.

items.original_ja: 彼の声には底力がある。
items.original_en: He has a deep voice.
items.corrected_en: He has a powerful voice.
items.notes: Japanese is good; fixed English mistranslation (底力がある means powerful/resonant, whereas 'deep voice' is 低い声).

items.original_en: I shook my head a few times.
items.corrected_ja: 朝からずっと頭が痛い。
items.corrected_en: I've had a headache all morning.
items.notes: 'I shook my head' is 首を振った in natural Japanese, not 頭を振った (which is translationese). Replaced with natural colloquial Japanese.

items.original_ja: その車は門を通り抜けた。
items.original_en: The car passed through a gate.
items.corrected_en: The car passed through the gate.
items.notes: Confirmed.

items.original_ja: 岡の上に寺があります。
items.original_en: There is a temple on top of the hill.
items.corrected_en: There's a temple on top of the hill.
items.notes: In spoken Japanese, bare 寺 sounds abrupt; お寺 is much more natural.

items.original_en: I have trouble with my bowels.
items.corrected_ja: なんか今日、お腹の調子が悪いんだよね。
items.corrected_en: My stomach's been acting up today.
items.notes: Nobody says 腸の具合が悪い in everyday conversation unless talking clinically; お腹の調子が悪い (or 体調が悪い) is how people actually talk.

items.original_en: Paper is made from wood.
items.notes: Confirmed.

items.original_en: Man is as fickle as autumn weather.
items.corrected_ja: すっかり秋らしくなってきたね。
items.corrected_en: It's really starting to feel like autumn, isn't it?
items.notes: Replaced old proverb fragment with a classic, natural seasonal remark people actually use in conversation.

items.original_en: Bamboo stands out in the woods.
items.corrected_ja: 家の裏に小さな林がある。
items.corrected_en: There are small woods behind the house.
items.notes: 林に竹が目立つ is unnatural phrasing.

items.original_ja: 彼は顔付きが良い人です。
items.original_en: He is a good-looking person.
items.corrected_ja: なんか今日、顔付きが険しいね。
items.corrected_en: You look pretty grim today.
items.notes: Draft error: 顔付き means facial expression/demeanor (e.g., 顔付きが険しい / 大人の顔付きになった), never 'good-looking'.

items.original_en: Sleep is better than medicine.
items.corrected_ja: 食後にこの薬を飲んでね。
items.corrected_en: Take this medicine after eating.
items.notes: Replaced stiff proverb with everyday colloquial usage.

items.original_ja: あなたは何人兄弟がいますか。
items.original_en: How many siblings do you have?
items.corrected_en: How many siblings do you have?
items.notes: Dropping あなたは and がいます makes it genuine modern conversational Japanese (何人兄弟？ / 何人兄弟ですか).

items.original_ja: 私は妹に辞書をあげた。
items.original_en: I gave my sister a dictionary.
items.corrected_en: I gave my younger sister a dictionary.
items.notes: Confirmed.

items.original_en: My sister has a very good brain.
items.corrected_en: My older sister is super smart.
items.notes: すごく頭がいい is great colloquial Japanese; updated the stiff English.

normalization_note: CR026 actual negative form normalized to 回らない/まわらない, explicitly accepted by user. Original submitted target_occurrence/correct_occurrence_reading fields retained.
